items.name: PostgreSQL
items.summary: A client-server relational database with transactional SQL, extensibility, roles, and server-managed concurrency for shared applications.
items.operations: Run and maintain a database server or use a managed service
items.best_for: Shared transactional systems with concurrent clients

items.name: SQLite
items.summary: An embedded transactional SQL database delivered as a library, using a portable local file without a separate server process.
items.operations: Application owns the database file and backup lifecycle
items.best_for: Local application data and workloads with modest write concurrency

items.name: MariaDB
items.summary: An open-source relational database server in the MySQL ecosystem, with SQL interfaces and deployment options for shared applications.
items.operations: Operate a server deployment or select a managed provider
items.best_for: Teams seeking an open-source MySQL-compatible database

items.name: MySQL
items.summary: A widely deployed relational database server with transactional storage engines, SQL tooling, replication options, and broad hosting support.
items.operations: Operate MySQL infrastructure or use a managed database service
items.best_for: Web applications that benefit from a broad hosting and tooling ecosystem

items.name: MongoDB
items.summary: A document database that stores BSON records and provides server-side querying, indexes, replication, and distributed deployment options.
items.operations: Operate replica sets and clusters or use a managed service
items.best_for: Applications centered on document-shaped data and flexible records

items.name: Redis
items.summary: An in-memory data store offering structured data types, persistence options, replication, and low-latency access patterns.
items.operations: Plan persistence, memory limits, replication, and failover
items.best_for: Caching, queues, counters, sessions, and latency-sensitive state

items.name: GitHub Actions
items.summary: Repository-integrated workflow automation using YAML jobs, hosted or self-hosted runners, events, environments, and reusable actions.
items.operations: Use hosted runners or maintain self-hosted runner capacity
items.best_for: GitHub-centered delivery workflows and repository automation

items.name: GitLab CI/CD
items.summary: Integrated pipeline automation for GitLab projects using YAML configuration, runners, artifacts, environments, and deployment controls.
items.operations: Use GitLab-hosted runners or operate self-managed runners
items.best_for: Teams managing source and delivery workflows inside GitLab

items.name: CircleCI
items.summary: A continuous integration platform using configuration files, executors, caching, workflows, and cloud or self-hosted runner options.
items.model: Hosted CI platform with configurable executors
items.operations: Manage configuration, usage, caches, and optional self-hosted runners
items.best_for: Teams seeking a dedicated CI service across supported code hosts

items.name: Jenkins
items.summary: A self-hosted automation server with pipelines, agents, credentials, and a large plugin ecosystem for customized delivery workflows.
items.operations: Maintain controllers, agents, plugins, upgrades, and backups
items.best_for: Highly customized pipelines under direct infrastructure control

items.name: Buildkite
items.summary: A hybrid CI platform that coordinates pipelines through a hosted control plane while jobs execute on customer-managed agents.
items.model: Hosted orchestration with self-hosted build agents
items.operations: Operate and secure the agent fleet used to execute jobs
items.best_for: Teams needing private compute with managed pipeline coordination

items.name: Azure Pipelines
items.summary: A CI/CD service in Azure DevOps with YAML or classic pipelines, hosted agents, self-hosted pools, environments, and approvals.
items.model: Cloud pipeline service integrated with Azure DevOps
items.operations: Choose hosted agents or maintain self-hosted agent pools
items.best_for: Organizations using Azure DevOps and Microsoft delivery tooling

items.name: Docker
items.summary: A container development and runtime toolchain covering images, builds, registries, local workflows, and daemon-managed containers.
items.model: Integrated container build and runtime toolchain
items.operations: Manage the Docker engine, images, networks, volumes, and updates
items.best_for: Developer workflows that benefit from a broad container ecosystem

items.name: Podman
items.summary: A daemonless container engine with rootless operation, pod concepts, command-line workflows, and integration with OCI images and runtimes.
items.operations: Manage containers through user or system services without a central daemon

items.name: containerd
items.summary: An industry-standard container runtime focused on image transfer, storage, execution, supervision, and integration with higher-level systems.
items.operations: Integrate and maintain runtime services through higher-level tooling
items.best_for: Platforms that need a focused runtime beneath orchestration layers

items.name: Buildah
items.summary: A specialized tool for building OCI container images from Dockerfiles or scripted commands without requiring a long-running daemon.
items.operations: Integrate image build commands into local or CI workflows

items.name: nerdctl
items.summary: A Docker-compatible command-line interface for containerd that exposes image, container, compose, rootless, and namespace workflows.
items.operations: Operate containerd and its supporting networking and snapshot components

items.name: Kubernetes
items.summary: A container orchestration platform for declarative workloads, scheduling, service discovery, configuration, rollout management, and cluster operations.
items.operations: Operate clusters, nodes, networking, storage, policies, and upgrades
items.best_for: Multi-service deployments that require orchestration and reconciliation

audiences.decision: limited team capacity and production reliability

audiences.name: self-hosted infrastructure
audiences.priority: control over deployment, data, upgrades, and failure recovery
audiences.decision: infrastructure managed directly by the adopting team

audiences.name: regulated teams
audiences.priority: auditable access, controlled changes, and documented operations

audiences.name: platform engineering teams
audiences.priority: standardized interfaces, automation, and shared operational patterns
audiences.decision: a reusable internal platform for multiple product teams

audiences.name: early-stage startups
audiences.priority: short feedback loops without premature operational complexity
audiences.decision: rapid iteration with a clear path to production

audiences.name: edge deployments
audiences.priority: resource efficiency, intermittent connectivity, and local autonomy
audiences.decision: workloads running away from a central data center

audiences.name: high-concurrency services
audiences.priority: predictable behavior under parallel workloads and contention
audiences.decision: many simultaneous requests, jobs, or writers

audiences.name: multi-cloud operations
audiences.priority: portable workflows and explicit infrastructure dependencies
audiences.decision: services deployed across more than one cloud environment

audiences.name: cost-conscious teams
audiences.priority: transparent infrastructure usage and manageable operating effort
audiences.decision: total operating cost rather than license price alone
